E.heading: The outcomes sought for the child or young person.
E.code_note: Paragraph 9.62 adds outcomes for adult life and shorter-term target arrangements. Paragraph 9.64 says outcomes are specified in section E. This assembler does not write an outcome.

F.heading: The special educational provision required by the child or young person.
F.code_note: Children and Families Act 2014 s.37(2)(c) and s.42. Section 42 applies where a plan is maintained. This draft is not a maintained plan.

lines.quote: A quiet space for a short instruction was described in this advice.

F.section_42_note: Section 42 applies where the local authority maintains an EHC plan. This draft is not a maintained plan.

G.heading: Any health care provision reasonably required by the learning difficulties or disabilities which result in the child or young person having special educational needs.
G.code_note: Regulation 12(2) says this provision must be agreed by the responsible commissioning body. This assembler does not record that agreement.

H1.heading: Any social care provision which must be made for the child or young person as a result of section 2 of the Chronically Sick and Disabled Persons Act 1970.
H1.code_note: Children and Families Act 2014 s.37(2)(e). Paragraph 9.62, section H1.

H2.heading: Any other social care provision reasonably required by the learning difficulties or disabilities which result in the child or young person having special educational needs.
H2.code_note: Paragraph 9.62, section H2, also mentions adult social care under the Care Act 2014. This assembler does not decide eligibility.

I.heading: The name of the school or other institution to be attended, and the type of that institution, or the type alone where no name is specified.
I.code_note: Paragraph 9.62, section I. Children and Families Act 2014 s.38(5) says the draft plan must not name a school or other institution, or specify a type.
I.draft_rule: Children and Families Act 2014 s.38(5). The quote is not copied. The caseworker leaves section I unnamed in any draft sent to a parent or young person.

J.heading: Where any special educational provision is to be secured by a direct payment, the special educational needs and outcomes to be met by the direct payment.
J.code_note: Paragraph 9.62, section J, is wider and covers a Personal Budget. Children and Families Act 2014 s.49. This assembler does not set a budget or a direct payment.

K.heading: The advice and information obtained under regulation 6(1), in appendices, with a list of that advice and information.
K.code_note: Paragraph 9.62, section K. This draft lists advice. It does not attach the reports.

timescale.exceptions_note: Regulation 13(3) says the local authority need not comply with regulation 13(2) if it is impractical for a reason in regulation 10(4)(a) to (d). This starter does not apply those reasons and does not find a breach.
timescale.regulation_13_1_note: Regulation 13(1) gives at least 15 days to make representations on a draft that has been sent. This starter does not send a draft.
timescale.counting_rule: This starter counts 20 weeks as 140 days from request_received. The regulations do not define that arithmetic. It does not know about section 24.

sources.title: Children and Families Act 2014, section 36
sources.notes: Section 36 is the EHC needs assessment. A request may be made by the parent, the young person, or a person acting for a school or post-16 institution. The local authority decides whether to secure an assessment. This starter does not make that decision.

sources.title: Children and Families Act 2014, section 37
sources.notes: Section 37(2) says an EHC plan specifies special educational needs, outcomes, special educational provision, related health care provision, and social care provision. The local authority prepares and maintains the plan where section 37(1) applies. This starter does not decide that it applies.

sources.title: Children and Families Act 2014, section 38
sources.notes: Section 38(5) says the draft EHC plan sent to the parent or young person must not name a school or other institution, or specify a type of school or other institution. Quotes tagged as section I are not copied into this draft.

sources.title: Children and Families Act 2014, section 42
sources.notes: Section 42 is the duty to secure specified special educational provision, and for the responsible commissioning body to arrange specified health care provision, where the local authority maintains an EHC plan. This draft is not a maintained plan. provision_secured stays false.

sources.title: Children and Families Act 2014, sections 37 to 49
sources.notes: The crossheading page opened on 4 November 2026 includes sections 37 to 49: content (37), the draft (38), finalising where a school is requested (39) or not requested (40), section 41 approval, the duty to secure provision (42), the duty to admit (43), reviews (44), ceasing to maintain (45), maintaining after 25 (46), transfer (47), release from detention (48), and personal budgets (49). This starter does not take those steps. Section 36 was opened as its own page.

sources.title: SEND Regulations 2014, regulation 6
sources.notes: Regulation 6(1) lists the advice the local authority must seek. Paragraphs (a) to (e) are the gap check. Paragraph (f) is discretionary. Paragraph (g) applies where the child or young person is in or beyond year 9. Paragraph (h) is advice the parent or young person reasonably requests. Regulation 6(4) allows existing advice to be reused where everyone is satisfied it is sufficient. This starter does not decide that.

sources.title: SEND Regulations 2014, regulation 10
sources.notes: Regulation 10(4)(a) to (d) sets reasons a time limit need not be met, including a school closure of at least four weeks, exceptional personal circumstances, and absence from the area for at least four weeks. Regulation 13(3) applies those reasons to the 20-week limit. This starter does not apply them.

sources.title: SEND Regulations 2014, regulation 12
sources.notes: Regulation 12 sets sections A to J and, in paragraph (4), section K. Each section must be separately identified. Paragraph (3) requires preparation-for-adulthood provision in or beyond year 9. The headings in this starter follow regulation 12.

sources.title: SEND Regulations 2014, regulation 13
sources.notes: Regulation 13(1) gives at least 15 days to make representations about a draft plan that has been sent, and to request a particular school. Regulation 13(2) says the finalised plan must be sent as soon as practicable and in any event within 20 weeks of the request under section 36(1), or of the authority becoming responsible under section 24. Regulation 13(3) disapplies that limit where regulation 10(4)(a) to (d) makes compliance impractical. This starter does not send the plan and does not find a breach.

sources.title: SEND code of practice: 0 to 25 years
sources.notes: The GOV.UK publication page was opened on 4 November 2026. It was last updated on 12 September 2024 and points at the January 2015 code. Paragraph 9.62 says the format is agreed locally and that, as a statutory minimum, plans must include sections A to K, separately labelled. Paragraph 9.63 covers preparation for adulthood from year 9. Paragraph 9.69 is about shorter-term targets. It is not the section list.

sources.title: UK GDPR, Article 8
sources.notes: Article 8 applies where Article 6(1)(a) consent is the basis, for an information society service offered directly to a child. The UK text sets the age at 13. Article 8(4) says the reference to information society services does not include preventive or counselling services. This starter does not choose a lawful basis and does not offer a service to a child.

sources.title: UK GDPR, Article 9
sources.notes: Article 9(1) prohibits processing special category data, including data concerning health, unless a condition in Article 9(2) applies. SEND advice often includes health. This starter does not assert an Article 9(2) condition. The data protection officer does that before any live file.

sources.title: Harnesses in Copilot Studio
sources.notes: The GitHub Copilot harness is a Copilot Studio authoring and orchestration framework, not the GitHub Copilot service. Customer data is not sent to the GitHub Copilot service when agents run in Copilot Studio. The page does not mark that harness as preview. It describes skills, memory, file creation, and a sandbox. The standard harness follows the topics and rules the maker defines. Skills and memory are listed as 'Not a focus' for the standard harness.

sources.title: Overview of usage-based billing
sources.notes: For GitHub Copilot harness experiences, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model tokens, tools including knowledge and MCP, and the harness. Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the GitHub Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building, including testing. A diagram of ranges was on the page. No number from it is copied.

sources.title: Standard harness licensing
sources.notes: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence lets you use Copilot Studio to build agents for the GitHub Copilot harness. The same page says that, with that licence, classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams, or SharePoint do not count against the message pack or meter. Those two sentences are not merged. No pack size and no meter rate is copied. The page says the common currency changed from messages to Copilot Credits on 1 September 2025, and that the quantity per prepaid pack and the pay-as-you-go rate did not change. The quantity itself is not stated here.

sources.title: ICO Children's code, services covered
sources.notes: Direct fetch returned 403 on 4 November 2026. The page was not opened. The code is the Age appropriate design code. Whether section 123 of the Data Protection Act 2018 puts an internal caseworker tool in scope was not verified from the page. The data protection officer decides. This row is not a citation of page text.

sources.title: Catalogue row UK10
sources.notes: Not a Microsoft or legislation page. Autonomy A1. The caseworker authors the final EHCP. Stack in the catalogue: Microsoft Foundry, Azure, and Copilot Studio. This folder does not call Foundry or Azure.

differences.experiment_08: Experiment 08 proposes redaction of UK identifier patterns. This assembler calls propose and still sets output_is_anonymised to false. It does not copy the detectors and it does not release text.
differences.experiment_12: Experiment 12 inventories a document batch and can suggest a purpose. It does not file SEND advice under sections A to K. This assembler does not call intake.

experiment_33.note: Experiment 33 is the case-bundle summariser, catalogue UK09. A summary narrates a bundle for a reader. This draft does not narrate. It files advice the report already tagged, withholds section I, and blocks export. The summariser is not called.

limitations: This draft does not decide needs, provision, placement, or outcomes.
The caseworker authors the final text. This file is not the final plan.

Regulation 12 and SEND Code paragraph 9.62 set the section letters. Paragraph 9.62 says the format is agreed locally. Check the local authority's own template. Paragraph 9.69 is about shorter-term targets, not the section list.
A missing advice type is a gap in this file. It is not a finding that the local authority failed regulation 6, and regulation 6(4) is not applied.
Twenty weeks is counted here as 140 days. That arithmetic is not in the regulations. Regulation 13(3) exceptions are not applied. A marker is not a finding of breach.
The 90-day window is a freshness flag for this starter. It is not a statutory expiry of advice.
UK identifier handling is Experiment 08. The output is not anonymised. Names written out in words are not detected.
This starter reads the paragraph text supplied in the file. It does not attach appendices for section K.
